item.title: Cryptopals Set 1: Basics
item.description: Cryptopals is a set of cryptography challenges by the NCC Group. Maciej Ceglowski wrote a great blog about them here. They’ve been out for a while and I originally tried to work through them four years ago in high school. I got to about the second challenge and then was stumped. Now, four years and a CS degree later, I’m back at it! They’ve been a ton of fun to work on so far and definitely challenging. I’ve “known” academically a lot of the attacks covered but implementing them is a different story.

item.title: About me
item.description:
Hey, my name is Murad Isayev, and this page is all about me.

I’m a Master’s student in Global Software Development at Fulda University. I moved to Germany in October 2024, and I work at a bookstore to support myself. Technically speaking, Go is my primary programming language right now for learning and building. In the past, I have worked extensively with Javascript/TypeScript (Node.js) with the focus on both backend and frontend. I have also written some Java and C from project to project. Other than that, I use NeoVim (proud face) as my text editor.

item.title: What I'm Doing
item.description:
Updated: September 2026 • Fulda, Germany

This is my “Now” page where I share what I’m currently doing:

  • Education: I have about a year left of my Master’s in Global Software Development at Fulda University. I’m mostly done with my subjects. Now I just need to land a decent internship. After that, write my thesis to close this chapter.
  • Development: I have recently started to do Cryptopals challanges in Go. Great resource for learning cryptography and security vulnarabilities by actually building and breaking. So far, I have completed a few basic concepts (raw byte manipulation, frequency analysis, cracking XOR encryption).
  • Reading: Quit:The Power of Knowing When to Walk Away
This page is inspired by Derek Sivers and the NowNowNow movement.
